page: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, featuring 8 virtual CPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The system includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with 2000 GB of HDD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the h1.2xlarge exhibits lower-tier compute performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 883.18 falls in the bottom 10%, while the multi-core score of 4177.44 is in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench single-core and text processing scores are in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance, with read-only large block speeds at 38.02 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 22.65 GB/sec, both in the bottom 25%. However, the PassMark memory score of 1968.21 and LLM text generation speed for a small 135M model at 99.68 tokens/sec perform at an average level.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the h1.2xlarge offers a high volume of local HDD storage relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for workloads requiring large-capacity sequential data access without demanding high CPU performance. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on traditional HDD storage and older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits random I/O performance and compute-heavy operations, as evidenced by the weak PassMark database operations score of 2390.78 and poor Redis SET operations performance of 2.51 million operations per second. This instance is best suited for legacy storage applications, data warehousing, log processing, and large-scale sequential file storage.
